header.userPrompt:
Make the bank-statement AI category/merchant suggestions reliable. Today they are computed by StatementSuggestionsService (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala), called from ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction. In production the stored suggestions come back with every row having no categoryId and no merchantId, so the review page shows nothing. Root causes, confirmed by reproducing the exact prompt against real data:

- The model is asked to ECHO category/merchant UUIDs and is sent a BATCH of up to 40 rows in one call. At that scale Nova Lite is erratic and non-deterministic even at temperature 0 (identical input gave 19/38 then 36/38 on repeat runs), and the prompt's "if no category clearly fits, use null" escape lets it blank out many or all rows.
- There is NO deterministic tier: the service feeds history only as few-shot examples to the model, never as a direct lookup, so repeated merchants depend on a model coin-flip instead of the category the user already chose.
- A silent short-circuit: `if (toResolve.isEmpty || categories.isEmpty)` returns all-empty suggestions with status Done, so a bug where categories fail to load is indistinguishable from "nothing to suggest".

BUILD THIS (keep the existing draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions model/columns, the background job wiring, the regenerate endpoint, and the review-page UI behavior unchanged except where stated):

1. DETERMINISTIC HISTORY TIER (primary, no model):
   - Add a user-scoped repository query that, for a normalized row description, returns the category the user has previously assigned to rows with that same normalized description — among already-categorized rows (bank_statement_row.expense_id set -> expense -> its single category split). Pick the most frequently used category for that description; tie-break deterministically (e.g. most recent). It MUST be user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?) and have a stable ORDER BY. Normalize descriptions with the SAME normalization the rule matcher uses (reuse a shared normalize, do not invent a second one).
   - In StatementSuggestionsService, for each row to resolve: FIRST try this history lookup; if it yields a category, use it directly (no model call). Only rows with no rule and no history go to the model. This makes repeated merchants deterministic and stable across regenerations.

2. PER-ROW, NAME-IN / NAME-OUT MODEL CALLS (replace the batch + UUIDs):
   - Call the model ONE ROW AT A TIME (remove the BatchSize batching). Sequential is fine and preferred (the demo account throttles Bedrock under bursts); it is cheap, just slower.
   - Send the category NAMES (with the existing few-shot examples), not ids, and ask the model to return the single best category NAME. Map the returned name back to a category id server-side, matching case- AND accent-insensitively. Do NOT offer a null option for the category — force a best-guess pick (the suggestion is advisory and the user reviews it before importing).
   - Then, if a category resolved and that category has merchants, send that category's merchant NAMES and ask for the best merchant NAME or "none"; map back the same way. null/none IS allowed for merchant.
   - Mapping back must be unambiguous: if a returned name matches no candidate, or matches more than one (the data has a real near-duplicate category pair "Super"/"Súper", and merchants may share a name), treat it as no match (None) rather than guessing. The chosen merchant's category stays authoritative over the predicted category, as today.
   - Keep failing loud on unparseable model output (as today).

3. FIX THE SILENT SHORT-CIRCUIT:
   - `toResolve.isEmpty` is a legitimate no-op: store status Done with an empty rows list.
   - But if there ARE rows to resolve and the user's categories come back empty, do NOT silently store all-empty suggestions — log an error with the userId and FAIL the job (throw), so a categories-not-loading bug surfaces and retries instead of masquerading as "Done, no suggestions". Confirm categories are loaded for the statement's owner (statement.userId).

4. SHARE THE RULE-BASED ROW RESOLUTION:
   - The rule MATCHER (ImportRuleMatcher) already lives in lib/api/shared and is used by both sides — keep using it. The thing that is NOT shared is the higher-level "given rules + a row, what does a rule decide for it" logic: the web review page (BankStatementReviewPage.resolveImport) and the server (StatementSuggestionsService.selectRowsToResolve) each have their own. Extract a single shared helper into lib/api/shared (next to ImportRuleMatcher — NOT lib/common/shared, because it depends on the api models) that answers the rule verdict for a row, and have BOTH the web review page and the server service use it. Do not reimplement rule matching separately on either side. This is a refactor with no behavior change to the rule path.

CONSTRAINTS:
- User-scoped DB access (WHERE user_id = ?) on the new query; stable ORDER BY; no CHECK constraints.
- No silent defaults for missing data — fail loud (the short-circuit fix above is an instance).
- Log the new/changed work with the userId in scope (per the coding-patterns reviewer rule), after the user is resolved.
- Use Chimney for any case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a Future.
- Keep changes surgical; do not restyle unrelated UI or change the draft->confirm flow.
- Follow docs/guide conventions. Add/adjust tests for: the history-lookup repository query (user-scoped, picks the most-used category, normalization, ignores other users), the service (history-first: a row with history skips the model; a row without history calls the model once; name mapped back to id; an ambiguous/unknown name becomes None; category is forced with no null; merchant allows none; categories-empty-with-rows fails loud), and the shared rule-resolution helper.

resultJson.description:
Make the AI category/merchant suggestions on confirmed bank statements reliable. Today `StatementSuggestionsService` sends up to 40 rows per Bedrock call and asks Nova Lite to echo category and merchant UUIDs, with an "if nothing clearly fits, use null" escape. In production that blanks out many or all rows, and the results change between runs even at temperature 0. History is only used as few-shot examples, so a merchant the user has already categorized depends on a model coin-flip. Separately, `toResolve.isEmpty || categories.isEmpty` stores all-empty suggestions as Done, which hides bugs where categories fail to load.

The fix has three tiers per debit row: (1) an import rule handles it, using one shared rule-verdict helper in `lib/api/shared` that both the server and the web review page call; (2) otherwise a deterministic, user-scoped history lookup returns the category the user most often gave rows with the same normalized description, with no model call; (3) otherwise one model call per row, in sequence, picks a category by NAME with no null option, then a merchant by NAME among that category's merchants, where "none" is allowed. Names map back to ids server-side, case- and accent-insensitively, and only on exactly one match. Unknown or ambiguous names (the real "Super"/"Súper" pair) become None. If there are rows to resolve and the user has no categories, the job logs an error with the userId and fails, so it records Failed and retries.

These stay unchanged: the `AiSuggestions` model and its columns, the background-job wiring, the regenerate endpoint, the draft→confirm flow and the review-page UI. The chosen merchant's category still overrides the predicted one (`finalSuggestion`), and unparseable model output still fails the Future.

tasks.title: Shared rule-verdict helper used by both the review page and the suggestions service
tasks.description:
Create `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/RowRuleVerdict.scala` next to ImportRuleMatcher. It is a pure function over `ImportRuleMatcher.findRowWinner` that answers what a rule decides for a statement-row description. Use a sealed ADT in the codebase's sealed-trait/case-object style, e.g. `sealed trait Verdict` with `NoRule`, `Ignore` and `SetMerchant(merchantId: Option[UUID])`, plus `def verdict(rules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule], description: String): Verdict`. Keep the `Option` in SetMerchant so both callers' behavior is preserved exactly. The server skips any row with a winning rule, even a SetMerchant without a merchantId; the web uses only a SetMerchant's merchantId as the rule merchant.

Then (a) make `BankStatementReviewPage.resolveImport` (web) branch on the verdict: Ignore → None, SetMerchant(mid) → rule merchant `mid`, NoRule → no rule merchant. Also switch the page's other rule checks, `ruleWinnerFor` in `isReadyToProcess` and the `findRowWinner` match near line 445, to the verdict, and remove `ruleWinnerFor` if that orphans it. (b) Make `StatementSuggestionsService.selectRowsToResolve` keep only debits whose verdict is NoRule. Change no behavior.

Tests: a new `RowRuleVerdictSpec` in `lib/api/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/`. Cover no rules → NoRule, an Ignore match, a SetMerchant match with and without merchantId, Ignore beating SetMerchant, and patterns shorter than 3 normalized chars being ignored. Subject strings name only the method (AP-TE-03). The existing `BankStatementReviewPageSpec` "resolveImport" tests and the `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec` rule-skipping test must still pass unchanged. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *RowRuleVerdictSpec"`, `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"` (needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider`), `sbt "testOnly *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: User-scoped category-history lookup keyed by normalized description
tasks.description:
Add a repository query that returns, for each normalized row description, the category the user has assigned most often. Do this with one bulk call, not one query per row. Suggested API: `BankStatementRepository.categoryHistory(userId: UUID): Future[Map[String, UUID]]`, with key = `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize(description)` and value = categoryId. Back it with a DAO method in `BankStatementRowDAO` (Anorm, next to `categorizedExamples`).

The SQL selects (bsr.id, bsr.description, bsr.date, ecs.category_id) from `bank_statement_row bsr` JOIN `bank_statement bs` ON bs.id = bsr.bank_statement_id AND bs.user_id = {userId} JOIN `expense_category_split ecs` ON ecs.expense_id = bsr.expense_id AND ecs.user_id = {userId}. Restrict it to expenses with exactly ONE split, e.g. `AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM expense_category_split s2 WHERE s2.expense_id = bsr.expense_id AND s2.user_id = {userId}) = 1`, and use a stable `ORDER BY bsr.date DESC, bsr.id`.

Normalize and aggregate in Scala with the shared `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize`. Do NOT write a SQL regexp version, because the spec forbids a second normalization. Group by normalized description and drop empty keys, since a description of only punctuation must not match everything. Within each group, pick the category with the highest count. Break ties deterministically by the most recent use (max date, then a stable id order). Keep the grouping logic as a small pure function in the DAO or repository companion.

Add no schema change and no CHECK constraint. Tests go in `BankStatementRepositorySpec` under a new `"categoryHistory" should` block, reusing the existing `createRows` / `link` / `createCategorizedExpense` helpers from the `categorizedRowExamples` block (lift them to class level if needed). Cover: picks the most-used category for a description; tie → most recent; descriptions that differ only in case or punctuation (e.g. "OXXO-123" vs "oxxo 123") share a key; rows without an expense are excluded; multi-split expenses are excluded; another user's rows are never included. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"`.

tasks.title: Per-row name-in/name-out model calls, forced category pick, and fail-loud on missing categories
tasks.description:
Rewrite the model part of `StatementSuggestionsService`. Remove `BatchSize`, `inBatches`, `validateIds`, the UUID-echo prompts and the `{"rows":[...]}` answer format. Change `resolve` to also take `userId: UUID`; the action passes `statement.userId`, which is the statement owner the categories are loaded for. For each row to resolve, in sequence (foldLeft over Futures, as today; never parallel, never a dropped Future):
(1) Send one category prompt listing category NAMES, each with its few-shot example descriptions. Map the `examples` (categoryId, description) pairs to names. The prompt asks for the single best category name and offers NO null/none option.
(2) If a category resolved and it has merchants (`merchants.filter(_.categoryId.contains(cat.id))`), send one merchant prompt listing those merchant NAMES and asking for the best name or "none".
(3) Build the suggestion with the existing `finalSuggestion` so the merchant's category stays authoritative.

Use one answer shape for both steps, e.g. `{"answer":"<name>"}`. Parse it with the existing `extractJsonObject`. When the output is not JSON or has no string `answer`, fail the Future with the raw response in the message, as today. Merchant "none" (case-insensitive) → None.

Add a pure `matchByName[A](answer: String, candidates: List[A])(name: A => String): Option[A]`. It folds both sides with `java.text.Normalizer` NFD, strips `\p{M}`, applies `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`, trims and collapses whitespace, and returns Some only when exactly one candidate matches. Zero or several matches → None, logged at warn with the userId. Make it `private[services]` so it can be tested. Do NOT use `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize` here: it deletes accented letters rather than folding them.

Short-circuit fix: `toResolve.isEmpty` → Done with Nil and no calls. If `toResolve.nonEmpty && categories.isEmpty`, `logger.error` with userId and statementId, then return `Future.failed(new RuntimeException(...))`. The action's existing `recordFailure` stores Failed and re-raises so the job retries. Include userId in every new or changed log line, including `logResolved`.

Update `MockBedrockClient.suggest` to return a parseable answer in the new shape, e.g. `{"answer":"none"}`. Otherwise local Mock-mode jobs would fail.

Rewrite `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`: the stub answers per prompt; drop the batching test and the "no categories → empty" test. Cover: one category call per row (2 rows → 2 category prompts); the prompt contains category NAMES and examples, no UUIDs, and no null/none option for category; the returned name maps to the id case- and accent-insensitively ("groceries" → Groceries); an unknown name → None; an ambiguous name with categories "Super" and "Súper" → None; the merchant prompt lists only that category's merchant names; merchant "none" → None; a duplicate merchant name → None; the merchant's category overrides the predicted one; no merchant call when the category has no merchants or did not resolve; unparseable output fails with the raw text; nothing to resolve → no calls and Done with Nil; rows present but no categories → failed Future and no model call. Keep the `finalSuggestion` tests.

Update `ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec` so its stub answers by prompt content in the new shape, e.g. a merchant prompt mentions "Groceries" and returns "SuperMart", and a category prompt for "SUPERMART 123" returns "Groceries". Add an action test: a user with rows but no categories → Failed is stored and `apply` fails. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"`, `sbt "testOnly *ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: History-first tier in the suggestions service, wired from the action
tasks.description:
Depends on the history query and the per-row service rewrite. Add a `history: Map[String, UUID]` parameter (normalized description → categoryId) to `StatementSuggestionsService.resolve`. In `ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.compute`, load it with `bankStatementRepository.categoryHistory(userId)` inside the existing for-comprehension and pass it through.

In the service, for each row to resolve, first look up `history.get(ImportRuleMatcher.normalize(row.description))`. Accept the hit only if the id is among the loaded `categories`; a stale id falls through to the model. On a hit, emit `RowSuggestion(row.id, Some(categoryId), None)` with NO model call: neither the category nor the merchant step. Only rows with no rule and no history go to the per-row model path. Keep the output in `toResolve` order.

Log a per-statement summary with the userId, giving the count resolved by history vs. sent to the model, and mark history-sourced rows in `logResolved`. The categories-empty fail-loud check still applies whenever there are rows to resolve.

Tests, `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`: a row whose normalized description is in history gets that category with zero prompts (the stub fails on any call); a description differing only in case or punctuation still hits; a history id not among the categories falls through to the model; a mixed statement (one history row, one new row) makes exactly one category call, for the new row only. `ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec`: seed an earlier statement row with the same description linked to a single-split expense in Groceries. The new statement's matching row is then stored with Groceries, and the stub is never asked about that description. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"`, `sbt "testOnly *ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/: Tapir endpoints and models shared by server (JVM) and web (Scala.js); this is a cross-built "shared" source set. `net.wiringbits.api.utils.ImportRuleMatcher` lives here: `case class Rule(id: UUID, action: ImportRuleAction, pattern: String, merchantId: Option[UUID])`, `normalize(s) = s.toLowerCase.replaceAll("[^a-z0-9]", "")` (this DELETES accented letters, so "Súper" becomes "sper"), `findRowWinner(rules, description): Option[Rule]` (ignore beats set_merchant; longest pattern wins; patterns under 3 normalized chars are skipped), `findReceiptWinner`. Tests: lib/api/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcherSpec.scala. `ImportRuleAction` (api.models.merchants) is a sealed abstract class with case objects `SetMerchant` and `Ignore` and an `entryName`; that is the codebase's enum style. `AiSuggestions(status: AiSuggestionsStatus, model: String, rows: List[AiSuggestions.RowSuggestion])`, `RowSuggestion(rowId: UUID, categoryId: Option[UUID], merchantId: Option[UUID])`, status Pending/Done/Failed (api.models.bankstatements). Do not change these.
- server/: Play backend, organized as controllers → actions → repositories (Anorm DAOs).
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala: `class StatementSuggestionsService @Inject()(bedrockClient: BedrockClient)(implicit ec)`. `resolve(statementId, modelId, rows: List[BankStatementRow], rules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule], merchants: List[Merchant], categories: List[Category], examples: List[(UUID, String)]): Future[AiSuggestions]`. The companion has `selectRowsToResolve` (debits = amount < 0, no rule winner), `finalSuggestion(rowId, predictedCategoryId, chosenMerchantId, merchants)` (the merchant's category is authoritative), `extractJsonObject` (strips markdown fences and prose), `oneLine`, and `CategoryField`/`MerchantField` constants used by ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec. The service touches no DB.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala: the background job `apply(bankStatementId)`. It runs `findInternal` → `compute` (loads rows, importRules.all(userId), merchants.all(userId), categories.all(userId), categorizedRowExamples(userId, 3), maps rules with Chimney `transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]`, then calls the service) → `store` (setAiSuggestions). On any NonFatal error, `recordFailure` stores `AiSuggestions(Failed, modelId, Nil)` and re-raises, so the executor retries. `userId = statement.userId`.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/{BedrockClient,RealBedrockClient,MockBedrockClient}.scala: `trait BedrockClient { def suggest(prompt: String): Future[String] }`. Real calls Converse at temperature 0 with config.suggestionsModelId. Mock currently returns `{"rows":[]}` and must return the new answer shape.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala: every method is `Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => DAO.x(...) } }` (RULE-BE-005: wrap, never compose Futures inside). `categorizedRowExamples(userId, perCategory)` delegates to `BankStatementRowDAO.categorizedExamples`.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementRowDAO.scala: Anorm `SQL"""..."""` with `${userId.toString}::UUID` interpolation, parsers built like `(get[UUID]("category_id") ~ str("description")).map { case a ~ b => ... }`, `.as(parser.*)`. `categorizedExamples` is the model for the new history query. It joins bank_statement (bs.user_id) and expense_category_split (ecs.user_id), ordered by `date DESC, id`.
  - Schema: bank_statement_row(id, bank_statement_id, index, date, amount, description, expense_id, refund_id, ignored_at, ...); bank_statement(id, user_id, ...); expense_category_split(id, user_id, expense_id, category_id, amount, UNIQUE(expense_id, category_id)), so an expense can have several splits. Evolutions are in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/. No CHECK constraints.
  - Repository models: `Category(id, userId, name, createdAt, updatedAt)`; `Merchant(id, userId, name, _, categoryId: Option[UUID], _, reviewed, createdAt, updatedAt)`; `BankStatementRow(id, bankStatementId, index, date, amount, description, manuallyEdited, confirmedAt, expenseId, refundId, ignoredAt, txnType, createdAt, updatedAt)`.
- web/: Scala.js + React (slinky) + MUI. web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala has the pure companion `resolveImport(ruleList, merchants: List[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant], aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions], row: GetBankStatement.StatementRowData): Option[ResolvedImport]`, where `ResolvedImport(merchantId, categoryId, categoryFromAi)`. Inside the component, `ruleWinnerFor(row)` and `isReadyToProcess(row)` (around line 233) and a `findRowWinner` match (around line 445) choose between the Ignore and Confirm buttons. Spec: web/src/test/scala/.../pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala, which unit-tests the pure helpers.

TESTS / CONVENTIONS
- Service spec: server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec.scala (AnyWordSpec, must-Matchers, ScalaFutures; `StubBedrockClient` records prompts and dequeues scripted responses, failing on unexpected calls; helpers row/category/merchant).
- Action spec: server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec.scala (`RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils`, `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => }`, seed helpers createUser/createCategory/createMerchant/createImportRule/createDocument/createStatement, sampleStatementMetadata; its stub answers from the prompt text).
- Repo spec: server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala. Its `"categorizedRowExamples"` block defines `createCategorizedExpense(userId, categoryId)` (Expense.Create plus one ExpenseCategorySplit via repositories.expenses.create), `createRows(userId, descriptions)` (row i on 2024-01-(i+1)) and `link(row, userId, categoryId)` (setRowExpenseIdForUser). Reuse them; for a multi-split expense, pass two splits to repositories.expenses.create.
- Spec subjects name only the method, never `"Class.method"` (AP-TE-03). Never use `var x = _`; use `uninitialized`.
- Every query on a user-owned table filters by user_id (AP-DB-01) and has a stable ORDER BY.
- Logging (RULE-BE-007 plus the reviewer rule): log user-scoped work with the userId once it is known; never log secrets. Fail loud with `RuntimeException` (AP-BE-01 style) and never default missing data. Use Chimney for case-class mapping (RULE-BE-008). Keep actions flat orchestration with no inline business `if` guards (AP-BE-03); put conditionals in the service. Never drop a Future; run Bedrock calls sequentially with foldLeft over Futures.
- Verify with targeted tests only: `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Web tests need `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider`. Do NOT run the full `sbt test`. Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.

NON-OBVIOUS
- Two different normalizations, on purpose: history keys MUST use `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize` (same as the rule matcher). Model-answer→candidate name matching must be accent-FOLDING (Normalizer NFD + strip \p{M} + lowercase), because ImportRuleMatcher.normalize drops accented chars. With folding, "Super" and "Súper" collide, so a returned "super" is ambiguous → None. That is intended.
- Skip empty normalized keys in history; otherwise all-punctuation descriptions would match each other.
- History category ids can only come from existing categories (the FK cascades on delete), but categories are loaded in a separate query, so filter history hits to the loaded category set.
- The server skips any row with a rule winner, including a SetMerchant whose merchantId is None. The web treats that case as "no rule merchant" and falls back to AI. The shared verdict must keep both behaviors, which is why it is `SetMerchant(merchantId: Option[UUID])`.
- RealBedrockClient caps output tokens; per-row answers are tiny, so that no longer matters.
- The repository memory notes nothing relevant beyond orca internals.

The full suite passed on the first run (`sbt test` exited with code 0), so I didn't need to change anything.

- **Command:** `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test`, run on Node v24.15.0 from nvm. That's the version CI uses (`node-version: '24'` in `.github/workflows/pull_request.yml`). The default Node here is v16.7.0, which rejects `--openssl-legacy-provider`.
- **Postgres:** Docker was already running, and the tests started their own Postgres container through testcontainers.
- **Results:** every test module passed with no failures — 36, 34, 36, 34, 173 and 710 tests. Full log is in `/tmp/fulltest.log`.

The sbt command ran longer than the 10-minute foreground limit, so it got moved to the background automatically. I waited for it to finish and checked the exit code before reporting this.

resultJson.title: Make bank-statement category/merchant suggestions reliable
resultJson.body:
In production, stored statement suggestions came back with no category and no merchant on every row. There were three causes. The model got batches of up to 40 rows and had to echo UUIDs back, with a "use null" escape it could take. History was only used as few-shot examples. And when categories were empty, the service stored empty suggestions marked Done.

- **History tier:** a new user-scoped query, `BankStatementRepository.categoryHistory`, maps each description to the category the user picked most often for it. It only counts rows linked to expenses with a single category split, and ties go to the most recent use. Descriptions are normalized in Scala with `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize`, and empty keys are dropped. A row with a history hit gets that category without a model call. Hits pointing to a category that isn't among the user's loaded categories go to the model instead.
- **Per-row model calls by name:** the remaining rows are sent one at a time, in sequence. First the model picks a category name, with no null option. Then, if that category has merchants, it picks a merchant name or "none". Names are mapped back to ids ignoring case, accents and spacing, and only when exactly one candidate matches. Unknown or ambiguous names (e.g. "Super"/"Súper") become None. The merchant's category still overrides the predicted one, and unparseable output still fails. `MockBedrockClient` now returns the new `{"answer": ...}` shape.
- **No silent short-circuit:** nothing to resolve stores Done with no rows. Rows to resolve but no categories logs an error with the userId and fails the job, so it is stored as Failed and retried.
- **Shared rule verdict:** the new `RowRuleVerdict` in `lib/api/shared` is used by the server's row selection and the review page. It is also used by `BankRowCreateExpenseForm`, `BankRowCreateRefundForm` and `ReconciliationMatcher`, which goes beyond the two call sites in the ask. These are meant as refactors with no behavior change.
